key_insight: A unified analytical model can diagnose where photoelectrochemical cells lose efficiency and translate those losses into concrete design actions across different device architectures.
engineering_relevance: The framework gives engineers a practical way to fit experimental J-V curves, compare materials, and prioritize upgrades such as better junctions, co-catalysts, or nanostructuring.
method: One model covers both BIJ and SEJ photoelectrodes using shared physical parameters.
It generates ideal and real current-voltage curves, efficiency maps, and Sankey-style energy-flow breakdowns.
Experimental fitting decomposes losses into thermodynamic, optical, recombination, and interfacial contributions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation against state-of-the-art literature across solar water splitting, CO2 reduction, NH3 synthesis, and solar redox flow batteries, plus comparisons between materials such as Si, perovskites, hematite, and BiVO4.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate experimental J-V fitting and physically meaningful parameter choices, so errors in inputs or model assumptions could weaken the loss attribution.
paper_title: From Loss Diagnosis to Rational Design: A Unified Analytical Model for Photoelectrochemical Cells
